The JAX host the HOU as favorites of 1.5, with the total set at 40.5 — a market that implies a JAX 21–20 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with JAX in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with JAX chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 1.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.
